description.narrative: A total of seven payments are made under this budget line to UN Trust Funds and Projects, reflecting the priorities of Ireland's international development policy, A Better World. These include UN Women-managed trust funds to support progress on gender equality and women's empowerment is in line with Goal 5 of the SDGs. For the first time in 2023, this budget line is being used to provide funding to the UNFPA's Suppliers' Trust Fund. A contribution is also made to the Office of the President of the UN General Assembly to support the day-to-day operations of the Office. Grants are also made to other UN projects such as the Joint SDG Fund and the Women's Peace and Humanitarian Fund, as well as a UNDP evaluative study on the SDGs.

The UNFPA Supplies Trust Fund supports programme countries to strengthen their health systems and to provide sexual and reproductive health services. The UN Trust Fund for Ending Violence Against Women works to achieve a life free of violence for women and girls. Women Count advances the production, availability, accessibility and use of quality data and statistics on key aspects of gender equality and women’s empowerment. The United Nations Women’s Peace and Humanitarian Fund (WPHF) supports local and grassroots women’s civil society leaders and their organizations in conflict and crisis settings worldwide. The Office of the President of the General Assembly is supported to carry out its administrative, logistical and management functions. The Joint SDG Fund objectives include integrated multi-sectoral policies to accelerate SDG achievement; greater scope and scale of activities to achieve the SDGs; and leveraging additional financing to accelerate SDG achievement.
